hints.title: Inverse Pairs Contribution
hints.text: Inserting value n into a permutation of length n minus 1 can create between 0 and n minus 1 new inverse pairs.

hints.title: Sliding Window Sum Acceleration
hints.text: The naive recurrence dp[i][j] = sum(dp[i-1][j-p]) for p in [0, i-1] simplifies to dp[i][j] = dp[i][j-1] + dp[i-1][j] - dp[i-1][j-i].

hints.title: Two-Row Rolling Modulo Dynamic Programming
hints.text: Track dp row of size k + 1 modulo 10^9 + 7. For each element i from 1 to n, compute new_dp[j] = (new_dp[j-1] + dp[j] - (dp[j-i] if j >= i else 0)) % modulo 10^9 + 7.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def kInversePairs(self, n: int, k: int) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        dp = [1] + [0] * k

        for i in range(1, n + 1):
            new_dp = [0] * (k + 1)
            new_dp[0] = 1
            for j in range(1, k + 1):
                val = (new_dp[j - 1] + dp[j] - (dp[j - i] if j >= i else 0)) % MOD
                new_dp[j] = (val + MOD) % MOD
            dp = new_dp

        return dp[k]
```

variables: N: number of elements in permutation
complexity.notes: Sliding window optimization reduces inner summation from O(I) to O(1).
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Unoptimized recurrence computes sum of size i at each cell in O(N * K^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Rolling 1D array updates in O(K) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use sliding window prefix difference to eliminate inner loop summation.
